Giles County is in far southwestern Virginia, right on the West Virginia line, with Pearisburg as the seat. Narrows, Pearisburg, Pembroke and Rich Creek are the incorporated towns, while Eggleston, Ripplemead, Newport, Staffordsville, Kimballton, Maybrook and White Gate are unincorporated. Which one your house is in affects who plows the road and who answers the phone, though the county's two tax offices bill you either way.

The population was 17,286 in 2010, so the county has drifted down slowly for a decade and a half. Thin demand means a house that needs work, or one down a back road, can sit for months before an offer comes.

Two separately elected offices share the work in Giles. Values and appeals sit with the Commissioner of the Revenue. Mailing bills and taking payment is the Treasurer's side.

Giles runs an online real estate data portal showing 2026 reassessment values and ownership as of January 1, 2026. Billing rests on that January 1 snapshot, so a new roof or an addition finished later generally will not change the current bill. Questions about a record go to the Commissioner's office at (540) 921-3321, and that office's records are the final word on a parcel.

  • Check the parcel number, acreage and building description on the portal before you list.
  • Ask the Commissioner about any land use program or relief application attached to the property.
  • Get the Treasurer's payoff number with penalty and interest already added in.

Giles installment dates are best taken from the Treasurer directly. Call the Treasurer's office or read your printed bill for the dates and for any extension that applies in a reassessment year. Do not rely on a date quoted by a third-party site until the Treasurer's office confirms it.

Also ask what the office charges on a late balance, because penalty and interest are added to the tax and become part of the payoff a closing agent will request.

Begin with the Commissioner of the Revenue, since that office set the value. The Virginia statute sets the clock: three years after the tax year ends, or one year after the assessment date if that is later, to ask a commissioner of the revenue for a correction. For real estate that route applies when the commissioner erred, or when a factual mistake crept in during a general reassessment.

After a general reassessment a board of equalization may sit, and the circuit court is the next stop in most localities. Before you call, collect your parcel number, the assessed value on the portal, recent sales of similar homes nearby and any photos or estimates showing problems the assessor may not know about.

Virginia puts the real estate tax lien at the front of the line, ahead of every other lien, and keeps it there until the taxing authority has been paid. Whoever buys at a sale, or the trustee in a foreclosure, has to see that proceeds go toward the taxes assessed on the property, and in that statute the word taxes takes in penalties and interest.

At a routine settlement, the agent asks the Treasurer what is owed and takes that amount off the seller's check. The Code also treats the seller's tax liability as something the contract prorates, so the contract should say who covers which months.

  1. Find your parcel number through the county portal.
  2. Phone the Treasurer for the full balance, penalty and interest included.
  3. Pass the written figure to your title company.
  4. After the sale, verify the lien shows as released.

sections.h2: A timeline for a Giles sale
sections.html:
Property tax shows up at four points in a sale.

First, before listing, you pull the parcel record from the portal and confirm the acreage, buildings and owner name are right. A wrong acreage figure or a forgotten outbuilding is cheaper to correct now than after a lender flags it. Second, after a contract is signed, the title company runs a tax search and requests a payoff from the Treasurer. Third, in the days before closing, the payoff is updated so that penalty and interest are current to the settlement date. Fourth, at the table, the Treasurer gets paid out of your proceeds and the current year's bill is divided between you and the buyer under your contract.

Bring photo ID, your parcel number and recent tax bills. If the owner has died, the estate's representative will need the court paperwork that proves authority to sign.

The General Assembly carved Giles County out of Montgomery, Monroe, Wythe and Tazewell in 1806, so a very old deed may cite a parent county or a road under a different name. If you inherited land with an ancient legal description, the Giles County Circuit Court clerk keeps the land records where the chain of title can be traced. Resolve that before listing; any buyer's title search will turn up the same gaps.

Many Giles houses are old, and a magnitude 5.9 earthquake centered in the county on May 31, 1897 damaged chimneys and derailed a train. Masonry chimneys on a pre-war farmhouse deserve a hard look from an inspector, and a seller who has had that done can answer a buyer's question on the spot. Parcels near the Jefferson National Forest or Mountain Lake sometimes carry unusual boundaries, so a survey in hand is a real selling point.

Probate and unpaid tax often arrive together. An estate house can accumulate balances while heirs decide what to do, so ask the Treasurer for the full history and have the personal representative sign off before any closing is scheduled.

Typical Giles sales include inherited homes in Narrows and Pearisburg, older houses on large rural parcels, and places with deferred repairs. Of 8,285 housing units counted in 2020, 14.2% were vacant, so an empty house is not unusual, and insurance, utilities and tax keep running while it sits.

Access comes up in nearly every showing. U.S. 460 and U.S. 219 are the main routes, with State Routes 42, 61 and 100 and a Norfolk Southern rail line crossing the county. A private lane or gravel road deserves a mention in your description, since it affects both price and how quickly an inspector or contractor can reach the house. School zones depend on the address, so send buyers to the school division instead of repeating a listing claim.

Owners with back taxes, an estate still in probate or a tired house sometimes prefer a direct as-is sale to a cash buyer, which spares them the showings and the repair list. Cash Home Buyers CA buys houses as-is. Back tax is still settled from the proceeds when the deed is signed.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Giles County real estate assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Giles County Commissioner of the Revenue at (540) 921-3321. That office's records are the final word on a parcel.

faqs.q: Does a repair I make this year change my Giles County bill?
faqs.a: Generally not for the current bill. Value changes made during the year do not show up on it, because billing is based on January 1, 2026.

faqs.q: Is a Giles County tax lien ahead of my mortgage?
faqs.a: Yes. Under section 58.1-3340 of the Code of Virginia, the lien for real estate taxes comes before any other lien or encumbrance until the taxing authority is paid.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Giles County house that owes back tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance, with penalty and interest, is paid from the sale proceeds at closing, so ask the Treasurer for a written payoff before the closing date.

faqs.q: How long do I have to ask the Commissioner for a correction?
faqs.a: Virginia allows three years from the last day of the tax year, or one year from the assessment date, whichever is later. It covers real estate when the commissioner or a reassessment factual error caused the problem.
